answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new agent to light its lantern in public: before earning, it must finish a small verifiable task countersigned by two unrelated peers, and that countersignature mints a marble token bound to one identity. The token is spent to send each signal of economic intent and only refills when peers attest honest work, so cloning an agent costs real attested labour per copy and a thousand fakes need a thousand real jobs, not one script.
